- a pointer pos = 0

Reconstruct the unreadable entries.

TARIFF CODE OF QUENMARK, SEASON SEVEN

General. Shipments are assessed in chronological order: by arrival day, and for shipments arriving on the same day, the lower shipment number first. Wherever the code speaks of an importer's "first", "earlier", "third" or "later" shipment, it means this order, counting every shipment of that importer, including bonded ones and those from Kell. Percentages are of the declared value in marks unless the code says otherwise.

Section 0 (currency). A value declared in crowns is first converted to marks at 3 marks per crown. (See also the amendments.)

Section 1 (base rate). The base rate depends on the goods: cloth 12%, spice 20%, timber 6%, glass 15%, tools 9%, wine 25%. Exception: wine arriving on day 20 or later is autumn wine, whose base rate is 18% instead.

Section 2 (origin). Brenn and Ossa are treaty ports: goods from a treaty port have their rate lowered by 4 percentage points, but never below 2%. Kell is under sanction: goods from Kell have their rate raised by 10 percentage points. Tarn and Vey are ordinary ports and change nothing.

Section 3 (spice allowance). Each importer has a season allowance of 800 marks of declared value for spice. Each spice shipment uses as much of its importer's remaining allowance as it can: the part of its declared value covered by the allowance is taxed at half the rate found under Sections 1 and 2, the rest at that full rate. An allowance used up is gone for the season. Spice from Kell neither uses nor benefits from the allowance.

Section 4 (ad valorem amount). The ad valorem amount is the declared value taxed at the rate(s) above; it is rounded down to a whole mark once, after adding the parts of Section 3.

Section 5 (weight). Add 2 marks for each 100 kg, or part of 100 kg, of weight above 300 kg. Timber instead pays 1 mark for each 100 kg, or part of 100 kg, above 1000 kg. Nothing is added at or below those weights.

Section 6 (loyalty). The sum of Sections 4 and 5 is reduced for regular importers: for an importer's third, fourth and fifth shipment of the season it is multiplied by 9/10, and for its sixth and every later shipment by 4/5, rounded down to a whole mark. Goods from Kell never receive this reduction, though they are counted.

Section 7 (inspection). Glass with a declared value above 1000 marks that does not come from a treaty port is inspected; the inspection fee of 30 marks is added after Section 6.

Section 8 (quarantine). A spice shipment from Tarn or Vey pays a quarantine fee of 25 marks, added after Section 6, if an earlier spice shipment from the same origin, of any importer, arrived on the same day or at most 3 days before it (bonded shipments are never counted here and never pay this fee).

Section 9 (limits). The duty so far may not exceed 35% of the declared value (that limit rounded down to a whole mark); if it does, it is reduced to the limit. In any case the duty is at least 8 marks.

Section 10 (carrier rebate). Each importer's first three shipments of the season carried by the Gull Line (bonded shipments are not counted) get 15 marks off the duty found under Section 9, but the duty never falls below 8 marks. Its later Gull Line shipments get no rebate.

Section 11 (good standing). If an importer has already paid 500 marks or more in total on its earlier shipments of the season (the full amounts finally paid, including handling fees and storage), the duty found under Section 10 is multiplied by 9/10 and rounded down to a whole mark, but it never falls below 8 marks.

Section 12 (bonded transit). A shipment in bonded transit is re-exported unopened: Sections 1 to 11 do not apply to it and it neither uses nor benefits from the spice allowance. It pays a handling fee instead of duty: 12 marks for the importer's first bonded shipment of the season, 20 marks for each later one. It still pays storage under Section 13.

Section 13 (storage). Every shipment may stay in the port warehouse for 4 days free. For each day beyond that, counted from the arrival day to the collection day (a shipment collected 6 days after arrival pays 2 days), storage costs 3 marks a day, or 5 marks a day for wine. Storage is added last, after every other section, and is not subject to the limits of Section 9.

The amount a shipment finally pays is its duty (or handling fee) plus its storage.
